newsitem.title: USA: HOT STOCKS HIGHLIGHTS - U.S. Corporate Earnings.
newsitem.headline: HOT STOCKS HIGHLIGHTS - U.S. Corporate Earnings.

text.p: WILLIAMS COS INC off 2-7/8 to 43-1/2 in heavy trade
Shares slumped after the Tulsa, Okla., natural gas company posted earnings per share of $0.64 a share, short of Wall Street's expectations for profits of $0.68 a share.

The company said operating profit at its Williams Interstate Natural Gas Systems business, which accounts for about half of the company's revenues, fell to $29.2 million from 1996's $32.2 million. It said the decrease was due to the loss of revenue from its south-end facilities which were sold in 1996. It also cited adjustments to rate refund accruals.
SCOTT'S LIQUID GOLD SHARE UP 3/8 TO 2

Shares rose 23 percent after the maker of household chemical products turned a first-quarter profit of $0.08 compared with a loss of $0.06 last year. Sales grew 12.3 percent over last year with a 25 percent jump in skin care product sales. However, Scott's said a cutback in advertising felled sales of its flagship Scott's Liquid Gold for wood product, with sales off 8.7 percent in the quarter.

The Cleveland-based company posted a loss for the fiscal second quarter ended March 31 with sales slipping to $28.1 million from $30.0 million last year. But the company said it expects to return to profitability in the third quarter. The company also said it believes "the worst of the semiconductor capital equipment industry slump may be behind us."

Shares rose nearly 10 percent after the Ohio insurance company posted operating earnings per share of $1.05 compared with $0.78. Net premiums in the quarter rose to $1.05 billion compared with $810.2 million last year.
Shares rose eight percent after the computer system maker earned $0.32 a share in the fiscal second quarter ended March 31, 1997, beating analysts' estimates by a nickel.

Coastcast shares dropped 17 percent after company's first quarter earnings missed analysts' estimates by a nickel. The company earned $0.13 a share in the first quarter, sharply below the $0.39 it earned last year. According to First Call, Wall Street analysts had expected it to earn $0.18 a share.
Shares of the sunglass maker lost almost 10 percent. Earnings came in at a penny a share compared with $0.15 last year; analysts had expected earnings of $0.03 a share.
